seo_description: Three Wwise middleware projects: voice management in a zombie shooter, spatial audio in a platformer, and cross-platform memory optimization.
hero.title: Three Wwise Projects
hero.subtitle: Wwise Middleware / Unity Integration / Voice Limits, Spatial Audio, Memory Budgets
about.text: Three school projects where I learned Wwise by hitting real limits. Voice limits in a zombie shooter. Zone-based audio transitions in a platformer. Fitting everything into 15 MB on Android. Solo projects from DAE (2021-2024). Not shipped games, but I treated them seriously: tracked memory, hit platform limits, wrote integration code.
boney.title: Boney Boogaloo
boney.desc: Zombie wave shooter, first time using Wwise. Kept hitting the 256 voice limit. Built random containers (6 shot variants, 6 spawn sounds), balanced volumes in Wwise, trimmed silence, ADPCM compression. 44 sounds in 9 random containers.
ellen.title: Ellen
ellen.desc: Platformer with spatial audio. Wrote 10 attenuation curves for different sound types. Footsteps change per surface via raycast. Ambient crossfades between zones over 6.5 seconds through State groups. 4 reverb buses for different room sizes.
stomach.title: Stomach Aches
stomach.desc: FPS platformer inside a human body. Had to run on cheap Android phones with 2 GB RAM. Zone-based loading keeps only the current zone in memory (Brain 670 KB, Mouth 384 KB, Stomach 2.8 MB). Wwise Silence plugin saved 80% memory. Waterfall uses 3 RTPC-driven distance layers.
